utterances.text: That was his statement but taken out of context, because in providing a lengthy explanation, he elaborated his view of Bosnia-Herzegovina within the context of all the republics of federal Yugoslavia, and then he said if Slovenia leaves the Federation, if it leaves Yugoslavia, then we could still stay on or, rather, Bosnia and Herzegovina could remain within Yugoslavia. However, if Croatia leaves too, then there was no chance for Bosnia and Herzegovina to remain within the framework of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Croatia, as you know, announced that it would leave Yugoslavia too. That was no secret for Izetbegovic, that Croatia also proclaimed its decision to leave Yugoslavia. Did that mean that a sovereign Bosnia had to be formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: Though Croatia had announced its departure, the activities of Izetbegovic together with the president of Macedonia, Gligorov, were designed to form either a looser federation or some sort of confederation, and I think that in that context, I wouldn't like to enter into this part of the polemics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is no polemics. You mentioned the Izetbegovic-Gligorov plan. As a politician, you remember that plan was reviewed at Stojcivac [phoen] at a meeting of representatives of six republics and that Serbia, that is myself who represented Serbia at that meeting, accepted the Izetbegovic/Gligorov plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: No. You never accepted that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Look at the documents from that period and how can you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: I'm very familiar with those documents, and you never accepted the Izetbegovic/Gligorov agreement because otherwise that plan would have been adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it was subsequently rejected by Croatia, and you can check that out. Now, tell me, please. Could you please comment on the programme that was published in the newspaper Voks [phoen], an independent youth Bosniak newspaper, issue number 7, dated the 16th of October, 1990, page 72. I have a photocopy and an enlarged programme. It is a programme for the settlement of Bosniaks from Turkey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What has this got to do with the witness? Now, let's move on to something he can deal with.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This witness was engaged in the political events of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I asked him regarding the position of his party and Mr. Izetbegovic, who had, without any doubt, the formation of an Islamic state under the domination of the Muslims, and in corroboration of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you're going to make those sort of allegations, the witness must be able to deal with it. It's suggested that Mr. Izetbegovic and you, by -- or your party, by implication, were bent on the formation, intended the formation of an Islamic state under the domination of the Muslims. Now, that's what's being suggested. Is that right, as far as you know, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. It is not right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What was the intention or plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] President Izetbegovic and the SDA ever since its foundation felt that Bosnia-Herzegovina should be a sovereign and independent state with three constituent peoples and the citizens living in it. Therefore, that was our platform ever since 1990, and it hasn't changed since, as can be seen from our cooperative attitude towards the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. 1445. And is it true that in reaction to the decision that you took without the Serb deputies, that the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, at a plebiscite on the 9th and 10th of November, 1991, voted in favour of Bosnia-Herzegovina remaining within a common state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: That plebiscite was organised under the wings of the SDS party. It was not organised within the institutions of the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You're surely not trying to say that more than 90 per cent of the Serbs voting in that plebiscite, that all of them belong to a political party, that is, the SDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: It is highly questionable how many people took part in the plebiscite, because there was one party organising the plebiscite, controlling it, and counting the votes. No one else had any access.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you're calling in question the option to remain within Yugoslavia. Are you saying that that was not the option of the citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina who were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: If they had wanted to do that transparently, they should have done it through the legal bodies of BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it true that the Presidency of BH led by Alija Izetbegovic decided, on the 20th of December, to address a request to the European Community for international recognition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That was after the Assembly decision, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And even that decision was taken even though representatives of the Serb people in the Presidency voted against?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: I don't know that they voted like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. You don't know. And was the principle of consensus applied in the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: It is quite certain that the constitution and law of Bosnia and Herzegovina were not violated, but I am really not familiar with the rules of procedure of the Presidency because I was never a member of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And members of the Presidency representing the Serbs in those days were Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did they vote against?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it true that the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the 25th of January, decided to call a referendum on a sovereign and independent Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the referendum was held on the 29th of January, and the 1st of March?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The total participation was 63.04 per cent of the electorate, of which 62 per cent voted in favour of a sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: I don't know the percentages now, but I know that more than two-thirds of the electorate voted in favour of a sovereign and independent Bosnia and Herzegovina, which means that it was both legal and legitimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. 1445, if a total of 63 per cent participated and of that 62 per cent voted in favour of Bosnia-Herzegovina, how then can you speak of two-thirds of the electorate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: I said I didn't know the percentages, but there's no doubt that if those figures were not correct, the international community nor the European Union would have recognised Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was recognised as a sovereign and independent state.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I agree with you that that should not have been done under those circumstances, but the problem is precisely that it was done, and this will be easily proven. Is it true that the referendum was organised upon the insistence of Alija Izetbegovic at a moment in time when the regionalisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina was about to be adopted, and this was in the interest of all three peoples?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: It was not at the request of Alija Izetbegovic but at the request of the deputies in the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could there be pauses, please, between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking for pauses between question and answer for the speakers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true and correct that the tension that existed during the referendum throughout the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina culminated with the killing of the Serb Nikola Gardovic and the wounding of Radenko Mirovic, also a Serb, in Sarajevo on the 1st of March 1991, during a wedding ceremony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: Those two events have nothing to do with one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That was the first killing that took place after the referendum during the tensions that prevailed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: Killings happen today on a daily basis in all towns, including Sarajevo. It was nothing unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, for myself as a citizen of Yugoslavia, it really was unusual. I don't know what was usual for you for wedding ceremonies, but this was perpetrated by four armed Muslim attackers, and this gave rise to panic among the Serb population. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1445
utterances.text: There was no panic. The wedding itself was supposed to serve for an incident of that kind, because the people attending the wedding ceremony provoked all the citizens through the parts they passed through, and it took place at Bastasija [phoen], a district of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean to say that the people who were the victims of these four Muslim attackers were in fact responsible for having been killed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've been through this with other witnesses. This witness wasn't at the wedding, so no point going on with this. We must adjourn now in any event. We think you should have an hour and a half with this witness, which means you have one hour, ten minutes left tomorrow, Mr. Milosevic. Witness B-1445, could you be back, please, at 9.00 tomorrow to conclude your evidence. Could you remember not to speak to anybody about it, please, over the adjournment, until it's over. We will adjourn now until 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th day of October, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
